source_name: Payspot ME d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Licensed ME payment institution positioning itself as first-mover in innovative payment services (bill payments, domestic/international remittance, e-commerce, digital channels). Site carries service launches, agent-network footprint and price lists — direct evidence of new rails and retail distribution reach.

source_name: Montenegro Transfers d.o.o. (Altapay Group) — corporate site
why_relevant: Licensed ME payment institution operating a Western Union-branded remittance network described as 300+ locations; part of the Alta group, which also holds Alta Pay Group in the ME register. Discloses network footprint, partner scheme and send/receive pricing — a proxy for remittance-corridor volumes.

source_name: Capital Transfer MNE d.o.o. Podgorica (RIA Money Transfer principal agent) — social/corporate presence
why_relevant: Licensed ME payment institution running the RIA Money Transfer network locally. No standalone corporate site was found during scouting, so its Facebook/Instagram channels are the de-facto announcement surface for promotions, corridors and location openings.

source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE card-business spin-off) — regional processor site
why_relevant: Dominant SEE card processor / ATM-POS services vendor (self-reported ~600k POS, 9,500+ ATMs, 15m+ card transactions monthly across 16 countries), spun out of Asseco SEE in 2017 and owner of Monri since 2019. Its news and country pages reveal processing, acquiring-as-a-service and merchant wins that touch Montenegrin banks and merchants.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka / OTP) — acquiring & POS pages
why_relevant: Largest ME acquirer by its own claim (POS network since 2002, stated 4,000+ terminals). Bank-acquirer pages carry merchant-service conditions, terminal counts and card-scheme partnerships — the acquiring half of this cell is mostly bank-owned in ME, so bank acquiring pages are the substitute for standalone acquirer disclosures.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — e-commerce / internet acquiring
why_relevant: Active ME internet-acquiring provider for merchants; the page documents e-commerce gateway partners, supported schemes and onboarding conditions. Key signal for which processing/gateway stack is used for card-not-present in Montenegro.

source_name: MINA Business — Montenegrin business newswire (payments coverage)
why_relevant: National agency wire that reports CBCG payment-card statistics releases and PSP announcements in local language (e.g. quarterly card-transaction growth figures). Fastest surfacing of numbers that otherwise sit inside CBCG spreadsheets, and picks up PSP press releases with no other distribution.

source_name: Borba.me — economic/finance desk (payments policy coverage)
why_relevant: Local outlet that obtains Ministry of Finance statements on payment-market openings (e.g. joint ME–North Macedonia negotiations with PayPal on receiving funds). Reveals prospective rail entrants and policy blockers before any register entry exists.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (fintech commentary)
why_relevant: Industry cluster of ME tech companies publishing analysis on PSD2 alignment, instant payments and request-to-pay for POS/e-commerce. Useful for identifying local technology vendors adjacent to payment institutions and processors, and for early reads on domestic rail roadmaps.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Montenegro — SEPA accession communications
why_relevant: Official EU-side communication on Montenegro becoming operationally part of SEPA — a structural change that resets cross-border euro payment pricing and opens the market to EU-licensed PSPs. Anchors the timeline for rail changes affecting every actor in this cell.

source_name: CBCG — Platni sistem (payment system operations & statistics)
why_relevant: Describes the operation of the national payment system(s) and publishes system-level statistics. Establishes which rails PSPs can reach, participant lists, and settlement volumes — necessary context for interpreting any processor/acquirer claim.

source_name: Lexology — Montenegro payment transactions law commentary
why_relevant: Law-firm commentary on the ME Law on Payment Transactions and its transposition of EU directives (98/26/EC, 2007/64/EC, 2009/44/EC, 2009/110/EC). Explains what licence categories and disclosure duties exist, which is the interpretive key for reading the CBCG registers.

source_name: CBCG — Instant plaćanja (TIPS Clone) programme page
why_relevant: Central Bank of Montenegro's own landing page for the national instant payment system built on the Banca d'Italia TIPS Clone. Authoritative source for scheme rules, go-live dates, participant list, caps and fee ceilings.

source_name: CBCG — RTGS sistem (system description page)
why_relevant: Operator description of Montenegro's real-time gross settlement system: participation rules, operating hours, settlement model. Baseline reference for infrastructure roadmap tracking.

source_name: CBCG — DNS sistem (deferred net settlement) page
why_relevant: Description of the national deferred net settlement / clearing leg. Together with RTGS it defines the pre-instant clearing landscape that instant payments are displacing.

source_name: CBCG — Statistika: Platni promet (statistical data section)
why_relevant: Broader CBCG statistics portal branch for payment transactions; typically hosts card/POS/ATM and payment-instrument series compiled on ECB methodology.

source_name: CBCG — Saopštenja / press releases (EN and ME)
why_relevant: Primary channel for SEPA milestones, instant-payment go-live, scheme participation announcements. Confirmed to carry SEPA operational-membership and SEPA-application releases with stable ?id= permalinks.

source_name: European Payments Council — Register of Participants (SEPA schemes)
why_relevant: Authoritative machine-checkable list of PSPs adhering to SCT/SCT Inst/SDD schemes; lets you track exactly which Montenegrin banks joined which scheme and when.

source_name: European Payments Council — news/press on Montenegro SEPA scope
why_relevant: Scheme-owner communications defining ME's geographical-scope inclusion, operational readiness dates and scheme-country list versions (EPC409-09).

source_name: Banca d'Italia — TIPS / TIPS Clone Western Balkans communications
why_relevant: Operator of the TIPS Clone platform on which Montenegro's instant payments settle. Publishes onboarding windows, participating central banks, technical/governance notes — the upstream roadmap source for ME instant payments.

source_name: ECB — market infrastructure & payments (MIP News, speeches on cross-border/TIPS extension)
why_relevant: Governing Council decisions authorising TIPS Clone provision to Western Balkan central banks and broader euro-area infrastructure policy that constrains ME's options (euroized economy, no own currency leg).

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA alignment (TIPS Clone) project docs
why_relevant: Financier of ME's payment infrastructure modernization (EUR 8m). Project appraisal documents contain baseline/target indicators, cost structures and timelines rarely disclosed elsewhere — high-value quantitative roadmap evidence.

source_name: Visa Southeast Europe — Montenegro country pages
why_relevant: Visa's own country-level communications for Montenegro: product/technology rollouts (e.g. Google Pay enablement naming issuing banks CKB and NLB), issuer lists, acceptance initiatives.

source_name: Mastercard — Montenegro/regional news pages (mastercard.rs Crna Gora subtree)
why_relevant: Mastercard serves Montenegro through the Serbian/regional site in Serbian; this is where ME-specific product launches (Google Pay, tokenisation, issuer partnerships) are announced in local language.

source_name: UBCG — Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (Association of Banks of Montenegro)
why_relevant: Industry body with all 11 ME banks as members; expanded remit into digitalisation/AI. Its statements and legislation section point to sector-wide positions on payment-scheme and SEPA implementation, and to member/bank actor lists.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — 'SEPA in Montenegro: Benefits and Challenges' (law-firm briefings)
why_relevant: Practitioner analysis dating the ME SEPA sequence (geographic scope Nov 2024, EPC application Apr 2025, adherence Jun 2025, ORD Oct 2025) and flagging legal/compliance frictions for PSPs.

source_name: MontenegroBusiness.eu — English-language ME business/payments coverage
why_relevant: English-language secondary coverage of ME instant-payments and SEPA economics; useful bridge for analysts without Montenegrin, and occasionally surfaces bank-level competitive framing.

source_name: PrestoPay (Presto) — official site, blog and product pages
why_relevant: First payment institution in Montenegro licensed under PSD2 by CBCG (authorisation ref. 0101-7917-2/2024, 14 Oct 2024). Publishes product launches (Presto Multibanking, Presto Link for business, P2P transfers, QR bill payment, expense splitting) and regulatory notes. Earliest-signal source for non-bank payment rails, AIS/PIS use cases and merchant-side offers.
